question: Does a two-column passage versus a large notated field necessarily indicate different medieval manuscripts?
access: Web-reader extracted catalogue text; the page screenshot request returned Cache miss and was not retried. No manuscript image was inspected.

catalogue_assertions.title: Responsoriale et Antiphonarium de sanctis
catalogue_assertions.notated_fields: ff. 1r–132v and 135v–144r; 11–13 staves and text lines, four red lines
catalogue_assertions.two_column_fields: ff. 133r–135r, two columns of 47 lines; ff. 144v–146v, two columns of 32 lines
catalogue_assertions.hand: The catalogue describes ff. 1r–146va and the top of 146vb as early Gothic minuscule by one hand.
catalogue_assertions.two_column_function: ff. 133ra–135rb: Tonale, a treatise with musical examples, attributed in the catalogue to Bernard of Clairvaux.
catalogue_assertions.notated_hymn_section: ff. 135v–144r: Hymni in festis sanctorum; identified within the notated-field range.

interpretation: The catalogue describes a medieval manuscript containing a two-column Tonale and notated hymn sections within a span it attributes to one hand. Their different functions and the unverified column count of the notated hymns limit the comparison.
limitations: The catalogue does not explicitly state the column count for each notated field; a single-column interpretation requires inspection of the original or a more precise description.
The two-column section is a Tonale with musical examples, not a hymn section. It does not supply an exact functional match for Fr 25592’s dense hymn layout.
The original pages, original copying sequence, dates and scribe attribution were not independently examined.
This separate Cistercian manuscript does not decide whether IV.173 and Fr 25592 belonged together and does not remove the reported chronological disagreement.
